subject: LLM artifacts, benchmark links & latency playbook
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@healthlyte.com>, Susan Park <susan.park@healthlyte.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27 15:12 PST
Subject: Post-call recap + recommended models, bench links and next steps

Thanks for the time on today’s call — good conversation and a clear pilot signal. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we don’t lose momentum.

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: customer-facing summarization + extraction for clinical intake forms (low hallucination requirement, throughput during business hours ~200 concurrent agents).
- Data constraints: PHI will be redacted server-side, want Private deployment (VPC) for pilot and SOC2 evidence.
- Success metrics: extract accuracy > 92% on seeded prompt set; end-to-end p99 latency < 450ms for seq512 under planned concurrency.

Recommended model slate (shortlist we benchmarked against your prompt pack):
1) redwood-open-v2-7b-q4 (quantized) — cost-efficient; good extraction accuracy in our tests; verified steady-state throughput ~120 TPS per worker; median token latency ~28ms; p95 token latency ~180ms; p99 token latency ~310ms at seq512.
2) redwood-llm-13b-qa-pt (mixed-precision) — higher quality for edge cases; throughput ~45 TPS; p95 token latency ~240ms; p99 ~420ms.
3) fallback: redwood-chat-3b for cost-sensitive routes (lower quality but faster recoveries).

What I attached / shared:
- redwood-verified-perf-20261125.pdf (detailed runbook and per-model TPS/p50/p95/p99 tables)
- pilot-metadata-slate.csv (expected input shapes, concurrency scenarios, prompt variations we used)
- MAP_Healthlyte_v1.pdf (mutual action plan: deliverables, timeline, success criteria)
- Live bench viewer: https://s3.redwood.ai/bench/healthlyte/20261125/index.html
- Prompt set snapshot: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-prompt-sets-healthlyte

Early operational notes:
- We recommend starting pilot on a 2-worker Dedicated pool of redwood-open-v2-7b-q4 with prefix caching enabled (sizable savings for repeated form fields).
- Canary routing: 10% traffic -> 7b quantized; 90% -> current baseline model to monitor regression.
- Regression guardrails: we’ll run your seeded prompt set every 4 hours and surface quality drift in the Console.

Proposed next steps (checkbox):
- You: confirm pilot scope + sign MAP (I attached v1).
- Us: provision a VPC-private trial environment and share access + bench links (ETA 3 business days after MAP).
- Joint: schedule a kickoff to align test data ingestion and success gating (suggest Wed 12/2 or Thu 12/3).

If that all looks good I’ll loop in Grace (ops) to scope Dedicated capacity and Camila as program manager.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) Regression monitoring 
- When you say "seeded prompt set every 4 hours," what thresholds will trigger an alert? We need ops-level SLOs (e.g., drop in extraction F1 by >3% or a sharp increase in hallucination rate).

2) p99 under burst
- Our contact center has unpredictable midday spikes — can you share the observed p99 behavior if we double concurrency (from 200 to ~400 concurrent agents) for short windows? Any guidance on autoscale/bursting costs?

Also confirm whether the quantized 7b variant is available in Private (VPC) with the same perf profile or if we should expect degradation compared to Hosted.

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29 11:37 PST
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended models, bench links and next steps

Susan — great questions; answers below. Looping Grace so she can size Dedicated capacity and call out ops implications.

1) Regression monitoring & alerting
- Thresholds: we propose alerts when extraction F1 drops > 2.5 percentage points (configurable) or when hallucination rate (as measured on the seed set tagging) increases by > 1.5x relative to baseline. We’ll post the aggregated metric to your Console dashboard and create a PagerDuty escalation if the change persists for two consecutive 4-hour windows.
- Evidence: every run uploads per-prompt deltas and example traces to the evaluation bucket; we include a human-check queue for any example that crosses the threshold.

2) p99 under burst & autoscale
- Short bursts (3–10 minutes) at ~2x concurrency on the 7b-q4 variant produced p99 token latency increases roughly proportional to queueing: our bench showed p99 jump from ~310ms -> ~720ms when worker capacity saturated. That is expected without additional workers.
- Recommendation: enable burst capacity (automated + manual) so when concurrency spikes we add 1–2 extra workers. Cost guidance: a single extra worker for 7b-q4 at your target workload is cheaper than moving to 13b for all traffic — we estimate incremental cost ~ +18% per spike-minute vs baseline. Exact numbers in the attached PDF (see burst scenarios table).

3) Private (VPC) parity for quantized models
- Good news: Redwoods' quantized 7b (q4) binary is supported in Private deployments. Perf parity note: p50/p95 numbers are typically within 5–10% of Hosted for the same hardware; p99 can vary more depending on network and worker placement. Our pilot package includes a short preflight suite that validates parity on your VPC infra before full rollout.

Attachments & artifacts we added to the shared folder: 
- Perf runbook with burst scenarios and cost delta tables (redwood-verified-perf-20261125.pdf)
- Pilot metadata (pilot-metadata-slate.csv) — please add a few sample payloads so we can reproduce production-like shapes.
- MAP v1 (MAP_Healthlyte_v1.pdf) — minor updates: added a quality gate clause and rollback policy.

Operational next steps (revised):
- You: drop 3 representative sample payloads in the pilot CSV and sign MAP v1.
- Us: run preflight parity suite on your VPC (ETA 48–72 hours after sample payloads are shared).
- Joint: kickoff meeting to set ingestion hooks + initial evaluation window (30 minutes, preference Wed 12/2 10am PST).

If you’re comfortable with the thresholds above I’ll mark MAP as "ready for signature" and Grace will block capacity.

— Rafael
